newsitem.title: ITALY: No more sausage sandwiches, Italian inmate pleads.
newsitem.headline: No more sausage sandwiches, Italian inmate pleads.

text.p: An Italian man accused of being a member of the Mafia pleaded with prison authorities on Thursday for mercy -- no more sausage sandwiches.

"We've had enough of mortadella, we can't take it any more," Giuseppe Calascibetta, 46, shouted from behind bars in a high-security prison courtroom where he and others are on trial for the murder in 1992 of anti-Mob judge Paolo Borsellino.
Mortadella is a popular type of processed sausage from the northern town of Bologna.

"Ever since I got here the menu's been the same -- a sandwich with a very thin slice of mortadella and in the evening, when we get back to our cells, they give us a potato," he said. "The lucky ones get a little slice of ham."
Calascibetta's lawyer said it was unfair to expect prisoners to undergo lengthy questioning without a hot meal.
But the appeal for culinary clemency fell on deaf ears. Court president Pietro Falcone said he had no dietary jurisdiction.
